takeaway: Sartorius runs from the anterior superior iliac spine to the upper medial tibia and flexes both the hip and the knee.

question.text: Which of the following muscles acts as a flexor for both the knee joint and the hip joint?

lines.text: The sartorius is a thin, long muscle on the front of the thigh.
It starts at the anterior superior iliac spine,
runs obliquely from lateral to medial, and ends on the upper medial tibia.
Because it crosses both joints, it flexes the hip and it flexes the knee.
It also abducts and laterally rotates the thigh at the hip.
Rectus femoris is different: it extends the knee.
